name: Playing Together
description: What keeps running on a shared server, backups, and how to find each other.

pages.title: Playing Together
pages.text:
[#](FFFFFF)[#]() **Key points**

- Only areas near a player run. Machines elsewhere stop.
- **Chunk Loaders** keep a base or train running while you're away.
- One player in bed skips the night.
- The server backs up the world every 2 hours.

The world only runs near players. If one of you logs off or travels far, their base stops: farms, machines and trains in those [#](7A3C9A)[chunks](entry://glossary/chunk)[#]() freeze until someone comes back.\
\
To keep something running, build a [#](2E5AAC)[Chunk Loader](entry://industry/power_loader)[#]().

**Trains** stop when they reach unloaded ground. A Brass Chunk Loader on the train keeps the area around it loaded, and one at a station loads it while a train waits.\
\
**Mob farms** still need a player nearby: mobs only spawn around players, chunk loaders or not.

**Night:** one player in bed is enough to skip it, so the other can keep working.\
\
**Finding each other:** share a waypoint to chat from the [#](2E5AAC)[map](entry://home/maps)[#](), or check the other player's spot on it.\
\
**Dying:** see [#](2E5AAC)[Death and Graves](entry://survival/death_and_graves)[#](); a friend can fetch your grave.

**Backups.** Simple Backups saves a full copy of the world every 2 hours and keeps the last 10, in the **simplebackups** folder (next to the world on a server, in the game folder in singleplayer). Restoring one is in the server guide.\
\
The server can also back up before a pack update; see the server guide.
